~APPENDIX
GLOSSARY OF TEWS RELATING

A
TO GILL NETS
Weights are attached the net downwards.

GaX Net - A rectangular wall of webbing provided with a head rope at the upper edge bearing floats and with or without a foot rope at the lower edge bearing sinkers; the mechanism of capture being enmeshing of' the fish either in a single lumen or several lumens of the meshes at the gill region or any part of body between the gill region and dorsal fin. Surface Dr;ft z The method gear when it is allowed to layers of the hater in such rope of the net is exactly in of water. ~ of operating of the drift at the surface a way that the head line with the surface

the net is attached finally. to this rope for stretching

Mounting Twine - Twine used for the attachment of the ~webbing to the head rope and fo~ot rope. Float Line - The twine used for the attachment the master floats to the head rope. of

Brace Line - The line used for lacing the adjoining shots in a fleet prior to operation. Bridles - A folded rope whose ends are connected to the free ends of the head and foot ropes of the end shots of a fleet connecting the net to the boat rope or the fleet and rope. The length of the rope is at least twice the height of the net (See Fig. 1). the craft Boat Rope - Rope connecting bridles at the proximal end of the fleet. to the

Surface Set -- The method of operation of the gear when fixed for operation at the surface layers of the water in `such a way that the head rope of the net is exadtly in line with the surface of water. Midwater Set --_ The' method of operation of the gear when fixed in any region between the surface and bottom layers of water. Bottom Set - The' method of operation of the gear when fixed close to the bcttom layers of the water. Midwater Drij2 - The method of operation of the gear when it is allowed to drift in any region between the surface and bottom of the sea, Bottom Drift - The method of operation of the gear when it is allowed to drift close to the bottom layers of water. Shot Indicates a single piece of net in a fleet.

Fleet End Rope - A piece of rope folded and interlocked to the central part of the bridles at the distal end of a fleet forming two arms, one of which bears the master float and the other the master sinker (See Fig. 1). to the head rope Floats Small - Floats, attached meant to give the required buoyancy for enabling the net to spread up for fishing. Marker Floats - Floats specially used on the float line to fix the net at the desired depth. to the distal end Master Float - Float attached of the fleet end rope to enable location of the For night operation this is often fleet end. substituted or supplemented by providing a flag, floating lamp or a self igniting light in order to ensure safety of the fleet. Sinkers of the Foot Rope - Weights used at the foot rope to.enable the proper spreading of the net. Master Sinker - A heavy weight used at the fleet end so as to enable controlled drifting of the fleet in a drift net and setting in set nets. Horizontat Framing Line - The lines inserted through the lumen of the meshes at regular intervals to make horizontal sections in a frame n.et. Vertical Framing Line - The lines extending from head rope to foot rope passed through meshes in the webbing at regular intervals to make vertical The intersecting point partitions in framed nets. of this line with horizontal line is tied fast as mentioned above.

Fleet - A set :of shots operated by a gill netter which varies from 10 to 50 depending on the ground of operation and facilities -available on the craft used. Main Webbing-The for actual ca$ture webbing of fish. in a shot meant

Selvedge - A definite number of rows of meshes at the upper and lower ~borders and at extremities of the webbing fabricated with twines thicker than those of the main webbing. He d Rope - The rope or line to which the upper *e"ge Floats are dp of the net is finally attached. attached to thZs rope for keeping the net buoyant.

Foot Rope -- The

rope to which the lower edge of
